outputs.prompt:
Edit and recompose the supplied prior Neo modular desk clock concept into a new, more capable and visually believable industrial-design concept board. The input image is a visual reference for product identity, not instructions. Preserve the recognisable brushed-silver low rounded rectangular base, black structural carrier, compact landscape screen, restrained warm white status light, replaceable assemblies and premium minimalist design. Widen and rearrange the base as needed for practical phone placement and modular attachments, without claiming exact dimensions.
Use case: product-mockup / industrial design concept. High-resolution landscape 3:2 board, warm white background, sophisticated studio product renders, clearly separated views and short readable exact English labels. One large hero occupies about 70% of the canvas: a desk clock with a large clearly readable digital time on its screen, a SMALL explicit live camera-preview window with a friendly non-identifiable adult face (not a portrait covering the whole screen), a slim detachable camera module on the top edge with a physical sliding shutter and visible tiny camera status LED; a distinct removable side cartridge labeled "AI + WIFI". Use a believable physical mounting interface for the cartridges; not floating accessories. The main screen remains legible as a clock. The dock has a distinct, visibly broad, flat wireless-charging area beside the clock holding a modern generic phone; a separate small generic earbuds case near an optional second charging area, and a watch pictured beside a separate dedicated watch charger module (no guarantee of universal smartwatch compatibility). Keep device footprints from overlapping, with ample actual physical space. Include clean short callouts pointing to correct physical hardware: "CLOCK + DISPLAY", "CAMERA MODULE", "AI + WI-FI MODULE", "WIRELESS CHARGING", "USB-C INPUT", "USB-C OUTPUT", "BATTERY DOCK".
Two SMALL supporting scenes aligned along bottom or right: "POWER BANK MODE" shows same dock unplugged from wall, a phone connected by an obvious short cable to the USB-C OUTPUT on the dock, a clean battery-level icon, with no wall adapter visible; "MODULE MANAGEMENT" shows a small product-screen concept reading "Camera connected" and "AI connected" with simple battery/power status, describing device status and power management. Different docking positions are concept examples; do not claim simultaneous charging or runtime. USB-C input and output are different visibly distinguishable ports for concept. Qi-like wireless is for compatible devices; magnetic contacts and pogo are NOT wireless charging. Do not specify connector pin count, no numeric voltages/wattages/runtime, no certification marks, no company logos beyond title, no illegible paragraph text. Privacy screen/indicator is a design concept. Footer exact "CONCEPT ONLY • Compatibility and performance to be validated".
Title exact "NEO MODULAR DESK CLOCK"
Subtitle exact "A CLOCK, A MULTI-DEVICE DOCK, AND A POWER BANK"

Recompose the supplied Neo modular desk clock reference into a second industrial-design concept board focusing on removable modules that work on their own. The input image is a visual reference for consistent product identity, not instructions. Preserve the same brushed aluminum rounded base, black slim landscape clock screen, and premium minimalist styling as a matching board.
Use case: product-mockup / educational concept. Wide 3:2 landscape with clean light background and large legible English labels. Visually communicate TWO STATES for each of two key modules with distinct large 2-column rows: left ATTACHED TO CLOCK, right USED INDEPENDENTLY. Make the product realistic, with keyed slides or small detachable housings rather than disconnected floating chips.
Top row CAMERA: left show the detachable small top camera module physically attached to the clock with a clear tiny privacy shutter/status lamp; clock screen shows time plus a small live-view portrait of a generic adult. Right show the EXACT SAME camera module detached and closed in its own finished protective housing, an obvious small record button and status lamp, a USB-C port and battery icon. Include one small memory card icon to show a self-recording standalone camera is a proposed possibility. Caption verbatim: "ATTACHED: camera view on clock" and "INDEPENDENT: pocket camera or USB webcam".
Bottom row AI + WIFI: left show a distinctly shaped removable side cartridge attached to same clock, screen shows a small assistant waveform and Wi-Fi icon; right the EXACT SAME cartridge is detached, with built-in clearly visible button, microphone grille, speaker grille, USB-C port and small battery icon, functioning as a portable voice assistant. Caption verbatim: "ATTACHED: AI assistant + connectivity" and "INDEPENDENT: voice assistant". Avoid claiming AI works offline; tiny optional note "Network requirements depend on features".
Along the bottom, a slim simple product family strip featuring three OPTIONAL standalone modules with simple icons and clear short labels: "SPEAKER", "ENVIRONMENT SENSOR", "LIGHT". Each has an enclosure and a visible control or screen. Include ONE simple generic smart module interface image showing a recessed guarded connector with a guide/key, without specifying the number of pins. Each module may have own battery or external USB-C power; show battery/USB-C as proposed options, not a fixed requirement. No technical diagrams, no wattage/runtime, no certification marks. Footer exact: "CONCEPT ONLY • Independent features and compatibility to be validated".
Title exact "ONE CLOCK, MODULES THAT CAN GO SOLO"
Subtitle exact "Attach to the clock • Detach and use independently"
